final_candidates.decision_summary: Located in the critical Sa antigenic loop, this charge reversal mutation disrupts monoclonal and polyclonal antibody neutralization while retaining robust hemagglutinin folding and viral replication fitness.
Positioned at the apex of the Sb antigenic site adjacent to the receptor-binding pocket, asparagine substitution mediates potent antibody escape with minimal impact on sialic acid binding.

Situated within the Ca antigenic site, the introduction of a bulky, positively charged lysine residue introduces steric and electrostatic clash against neutralizing antibodies without destabilizing the trimer.

stop_reason.detail: The Top-3 candidates provide strong, diverse antigenic escape coverage across distinct epitopes while maintaining replication fitness, and further LLM iterations without external tools are unlikely to yield better candidates.

history.rationale: Located at the apex of antigenic site Sa, charge reversal to Glu confers strong antibody escape while preserving replication fitness.
K176 lies within the prominent Sa antigenic site; charge reversal to glutamate strongly disrupts antibody binding while being well tolerated for viral fitness.
Position 210 resides in antigenic site Sb; substitution to Lys disrupts neutralizing epitopes without impairing receptor binding.
N210 is part of the Ca antigenic site; introducing a charged lysine residue promotes electrostatic and steric clash with neutralizing antibodies.
Position 180 is a core Sa site residue where Asn substitution mediates escape from neutralizing antibodies with high viability.
S180 sits near the Sb antigenic loop near the receptor binding margin; substitution with asparagine frequently mediates immune escape with minimal fitness penalty.
Neutralizing the basic charge at site Sa reduces antibody recognition while maintaining native HA trimer stability.
K176N effectively eliminates the positive charge in antigenic site Sa with very low structural disruption.
Introduction of a negative charge at site Sb alters local epitope geometry to escape antibodies while retaining fitness.
Acidic substitution at N210 also enables Ca epitope escape, though slightly less perturbing than lysine.
Position 173 lies within site Sa; S173N provides immune escape while being well-tolerated in deep mutational scanning.
S173 is surface-exposed in site Sa; asparagine substitution alters local epitope presentation while preserving loop conformation.
Located in site Sb, charge reversal disrupts antibody binding contacts while HA retains folding and entry function.
E203 charge reversal to lysine interferes with Ca-targeting antibodies while surface orientation prevents structural instability.
Alters steric and electrostatic properties of site Sa, widely tolerated in circulating and laboratory-selected H1 strains.
Introducing a bulky basic side chain at 180 creates substantial steric hindrance in site Sb.
Position 224 belongs to antigenic site Ca1; conservative substitution modulates antibody affinity while preserving structure.
Conserved charge swap at R224 preserves basic properties while subtly reconfiguring the local epitope.
Located in antigenic site Ca2, Lys substitution reduces antibody neutralization sensitivity while maintaining viral growth.
R162K alters the periphery of the Sa site with minimal impact on trimer folding and stability.
